items.sentence: FY2022 revenue rose on increased deliveries of 19,412 vehicles, and FY2023 on 29,790 more deliveries plus higher average selling prices .

passages.filing: FY2022 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Revenues increased for the year ended December 31, 2022, compared to the year ended December 31, 2021 primarily due to increased deliveries of 19,412 vehicles.

passages.filing: FY2023 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Revenues increased primarily due to an increase in deliveries of 29,790 vehicles, increased average selling prices, and sales of non-Rivian vehicle trade-ins. Included in revenues for the year ended December 31, 2023 was $73 million of regulatory environmental credit sales.

items.label: supported
items.reason: P67 attributes FY2022 to 19,412 more deliveries. P56 attributes FY2023 to 29,790 more deliveries and higher average selling prices.

items.sentence: Software and services revenue rose 221.7% to $1.56 billion on vehicle electrical architecture and software development services for the Joint Venture, plus remarketing and repair and maintenance .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Software and services revenues increased significantly for the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily due to an increase in vehicle electrical architecture and software development services, as well as increases in remarketing sales and vehicle repair and maintenance services.

items.label: partial
items.reason: P18 cites electrical architecture/software services, remarketing, and repair/maintenance. It never says the services were for the Joint Venture.

items.sentence: Automotive revenue fell 14.6% to $3.83 billion as deliveries dropped 9,332 vehicles, partly from expiration of 45W tax credits, and regulatory credit sales declined .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Automotive revenues decreased for the year ended December 31, 2025, primarily resulting from a decrease in deliveries of 9,332 vehicles, due in part to the expiration of 45W tax credits after September 30, 2025, as well as a decrease in sales of automotive regulatory credits, partially offset by higher average selling prices and a higher mix of R1 deliveries. The increase in average selling prices was driven by a consumer shift towards higher performance variants along with a decline in discounting.

items.label: supported
items.reason: P22 cites 9,332 fewer deliveries, partly from 45W credit expiration, and lower regulatory credit sales.

items.sentence: The FY2025 bridge was almost entirely cost of revenue, +26.8pp, as Automotive cost fell on fewer vehicles, lower raw material and conversion costs, and prior-year accelerated depreciation .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: For the year ended December 31, 2025, Automotive cost of revenues included $484 million of depreciation and amortization expense and $43 million of stock-based compensation expense. The year-over-year decrease in Automotive cost of revenues was primarily due to fewer vehicles being produced and delivered, as well as reductions in the cost of raw materials, product components, and conversion costs, resulting in part from the cost of revenue efficiency initiatives and accelerated depreciation that occurred during the prior year.

items.label: supported
items.reason: P21 attributes lower Automotive cost to fewer vehicles, lower raw material and conversion costs, and prior-year accelerated depreciation.

items.sentence: SG&A cost 0.5pp of margin as go-to-market expansion raised payroll and stock-based compensation, while R&D added 1.5pp .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: For the year ended December 31, 2025, SG&A expenses included $221 million of depreciation and amortization expense and $324 million of stock-based compensation expense. SG&A expenses increased as a result of expanding our go-to-market operations and footprint, including higher payroll and related expenses primarily driven by increased headcount, stock-based compensation expenses primarily attributable to an increase in the total amount of accrued stock-based bonus incentives, and facilities expenses.

items.label: supported
items.reason: P13 attributes the SG&A increase to go-to-market expansion, higher payroll from headcount, and stock-based compensation. R&D figure is not a causal claim.

items.sentence: Net margin of -67.7% tracked operating margin, with other expense of $54 million including a $186 million litigation settlement .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Other expense, net increased for the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily due to $186 million of expense recorded for the settlement of securities class action litigation, net of expected insurance recoveries, which was partially offset by the cumulative gain on our equity method investment in Also, Inc. (refer to Note 16 “Commitments and Contingencies” and Note 2 "Equity Method Investments" to our consolidated financial statements included in this Form 10-K for more information).

items.label: supported
items.reason: P10 states other expense rose mainly from the $186 million securities litigation settlement, partly offset by the Also, Inc. gain.

items.sentence: The operating improvement came primarily from a significant reduction in net loss .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Net cash used in operating activities decreased during the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily driven by a significant reduction in net loss.

items.label: partial
items.reason: P4 links reduced net loss to lower operating cash used. The sentence's 'operating improvement' does not specify operating cash flow.

items.sentence: Financing raised $886 million, mainly $750 million of stock issued to Volkswagen Group, and the diluted share count rose 17.1% .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Net cash provided by financing activities during the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily resulted from the issuance of $750 million in shares of Class A common stock to Volkswagen Group in connection with the achievement of the Financial Milestone, as well as capital contributed by outside parties in the formation of Mind Robotics, Inc. and Mind Robotics, LLC (see Note 1 "Presentation and Nature of Operations" and Note 19 “Variable Interest Entities” to our consolidated financial statements included in this Form 10-K for more information). Net cash provided by financing activities during the year ended December 31, 2024 primarily resulted from the issuance of the 2026 Convertible Note (see Note 10 “Debt” to our consolidated financial statements included in this Form 10-K for more information).

items.label: supported
items.reason: P2 attributes financing mainly to the $750 million Class A share issuance to Volkswagen Group. It also cites Mind Robotics contributions.
